project.target_audience: Young adults interested in African heritage
project.visual_style: Cinematic documentary, warm earth tones, golden hour light
project.creative_direction: Respectful, educational tone; distinguish UNESCO-documented facts from artistic reconstruction.
project.music_prompt: Ambient Ethiopian-inspired strings and krar, meditative, 75 seconds, no vocals

metadata.historical_notes: Lalibela churches are attributed to King Lalibela (13th century); UNESCO World Heritage since 1978.
metadata.creative_notes: Interior lighting and crowd scenes are interpretive reconstructions.

loc_lalibela.description: Exterior of Bet Giyorgis church, distinctive cross-shaped monolithic structure

char_guide.description: Local heritage guide in modest traditional dress, neutral expression

shots.narration_text: High in the Ethiopian highlands, eleven medieval churches were carved from living rock.
shots.visual_description: Wide aerial-style view of Lalibela landscape at sunrise
shots.image_prompt: Lalibela Ethiopia rock churches sunrise aerial cinematic documentary
shots.video_prompt: Slow push in over misty highlands toward ancient stone churches
shots.subtitle_text_en: High in the Ethiopian highlands, eleven medieval churches were carved from living rock.

shots.narration_text: King Lalibela's vision turned stone into sanctuary—facts we know from UNESCO records, not legend alone.
shots.visual_description: Bet Giyorgis exterior with guide gesturing toward facade

shots.video_prompt: Gentle orbit around church facade, dust motes in sun
shots.subtitle_text_en: King Lalibela's vision turned stone into sanctuary—facts we know from UNESCO records.

shots.narration_text: Inside, pilgrims still walk tunnels and arches—a living heritage site, not a museum frozen in time.

shots.subtitle_text_en: Inside, pilgrims still walk tunnels and arches—a living heritage site.

shots.narration_text: These stones remind us: heritage endures when communities protect and share their stories.

shots.subtitle_text_en: Heritage endures when communities protect and share their stories.

shots.narration_text: Lalibela invites us to listen—to rock, to faith, to history still being written.
